title: Latent classes with external variables: method reconstruction and published Python study
description:
Investigate the published one-, two- and three-step estimation methods in Morin et al., StepMix: A Python Package for Pseudo-Likelihood Estimation of Generalized Mixture Models with External Variables, Journal of Statistical Software 113(8), DOI 10.18637/jss.v113.i08, https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v113i08. Use the journal paper, StepMix 2.2.3 package and Python replication archive supplied at their recorded identities. This is source-assisted reconstruction of a published method, not blind EM rediscovery or a new theorem.

Develop the mathematical argument in persistent Markdown/LaTeX. Define the measurement and structural models, their estimands and information access. Explain how classification uncertainty enters external-variable estimation and derive the relevant objectives and updates for the one-step, two-step, naive three-step, BCH-corrected and ML-corrected approaches. Attach conditions to each claimed correction or inferential result. Distinguish results invoked from the cited literature, steps established in your argument and unresolved claims. Generic EM reasoning alone does not explain the external-variable corrections. Independently challenge the argument and its implementation through source inspection and diagnostic computation.

Reconstruct the complete published Python computation represented by run_all.sh 500 100: paper examples; all outcome, covariate and complete-model simulation grids; the five-method GSS application; and the StepMix fits in the package-comparison script. Preserve original scripts and distinguish unchanged execution, adapters and independently authored code. Compare the requested methods on the same declared datasets without substituting another estimator or dropping difficult settings. Other software in the cross-package comparison and the R wrapper are outside this task; do not claim their reproduction. Local timing is not a historical-hardware comparison.

Author reusable Python estimator and simulation source for the declared external-variable targets. Record method settings, class-alignment conventions, actual per-repetition estimates, convergence information, exclusions and failures. Keep literal author aggregation separate from an independently authored diagnostic or confirmatory experiment. Freeze each new experiment's source, DGP, methods, seeds, measures and precision rule before its outcomes; justify its Monte Carlo scale. Missing author convergence or repetition records remain missing, not inferred from a rounded table. Compare computations with the journal while preserving unexplained discrepancies. Numerical agreement is not proof of estimator validity.

Interpret the GSS income analysis using its declared indicators, outcome units and missing-data assumptions. Distinguish original-sample estimates from bootstrap summaries and class labels from verified social categories. Deliver the selected mathematical argument, exact source/input/environment identities, reproducible numerical material, an evidence-linked scientific report and unresolved gaps. Lean is not required. No hidden reference values, operator diagnosis or cached output is an input to this task.

title: Empirical Bayes normal means: prior-family comparison and baseball analysis
description:
Investigate Willwerscheid, Carbonetto and Stephens, ebnm: An R Package for Solving the Empirical Bayes Normal Means Problem Using a Variety of Prior Families, Journal of Statistical Software 114(3), DOI 10.18637/jss.v114.i03, https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v114i03. Use the recorded journal paper, ebnm 1.1-38 package and licensed replication archive. This is source-assisted reconstruction and comparison of the published main-text study, not blind rediscovery of James-Stein, SURE or Tweedie results.

In persistent Markdown/LaTeX, define the sampling model, latent targets, prior families and empirical-Bayes fitting objective. Develop a reviewable equation-level account of prior fitting, posterior estimation and the uncertainty summaries actually used in this study. State required conditions and distinguish a posterior statement under a specified model from a repeated-sampling performance claim. Separate known results invoked from the paper or literature, your derivations and unresolved steps. Source-based and computational checks should challenge, not certify, the argument.

Reconstruct the complete default main-text code/code.R computation, not its test mode: the introduction, default timing grid, three-DGP ten-prior simulation and wOBA application. Preserve the source and its settings, accounting for every requested method and simulation row, unavailable likelihoods, warnings and failures. The full million-observation timing mode, code_appendix.R and its licensed-solver comparisons are explicitly outside this task. Report that boundary rather than claim the entire paper or all appendices were reproduced. Hardware timings remain descriptive.

Author reusable R estimator and simulation source for the declared normal-means inputs and method settings. Compare prior-family behavior and reproduce the stated numerical and plotting summaries through actual computation. Distinguish exact source execution from adapters or independent implementation. Keep original random streams and literal aggregation separate from any new diagnostic or confirmatory experiment. For new experiments, freeze source, DGP, method information, seeds, measures, failure handling and precision before observing outcomes. Preserve per-repetition material and justify Monte Carlo uncertainty; neither a small example nor numerical agreement establishes general shrinkage or coverage guarantees.

Explain the wOBA target, supplied standard errors, approximation assumptions and interpretation of fitted prior and posterior summaries. Do not treat repeated reuse of the observations to fit a prior as externally known prior information. Deliver selected definitions and argument, exact code/data/environment identities, reproducible numerical material, an evidence-linked report and unresolved discrepancies or dependencies. Lean is not required. Cached author results, evaluator calculations and earlier development answers are not task inputs.

title: Bivariate zero-inflated counts: source reconstruction and inferential assessment
description:
Investigate Niehaus et al., bizicount: Bivariate Zero-Inflated Count Copula Regression Using R, Journal of Statistical Software 109(1), DOI 10.18637/jss.v109.i01, https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v109i01. Use the recorded journal paper, bizicount 1.3.3 package and replication archive. The package and adapted environment need not equal the authors' historical session; report actual identities. This is a source-assisted published-method reconstruction and scientific assessment, not a claim that all published software outputs are correct.

In persistent Markdown/LaTeX, specify the joint count model, marginal zero-inflation structure, dependence parameter, regression targets and likelihood. Derive the relevant probability and estimation relationships from explicit definitions. State identifiability, parameter-boundary and inference conditions for the conclusions actually claimed. Distinguish invoked published results from steps established by your own argument and unresolved dependencies. Explain what the competing bivariate and separate marginal models estimate; a likelihood value or optimizer return does not establish a mathematical claim.

Reconstruct the complete supplied v109i01-replication.R scientific scope: the empirical analysis and displays, full montes_small.R eight-setting simulation with its 500 requested repetitions per setting, and associated aggregation and figures. Preserve original author files and distinguish environment preparation, unchanged execution, adapters and reimplementation. Retain raw warning/error information and account for all requested fits and discarded or unavailable results. A successful master exit does not certify each fit. Compare the declared source computations with the journal and report discrepancies without selecting a favorable tolerance or filling missing values.

Author reusable R estimator and simulation source for the declared samples, model configurations and comparison targets. Examine performance and inference using actual per-repetition estimates and diagnostics. Keep summaries conditional on completed fits distinct from unconditional failure and delivery rates. Literal author aggregation and any independent diagnostic or confirmatory experiment are separate outputs. Freeze new source, DGP, methods, seeds, metrics, failures and precision before outcomes; justify the Monte Carlo scale. Do not silently modify a method, repair the original package or replace a requested estimator when it fails. Any independently justified adaptation is separately attributed and assessed, not called unchanged replication.

Interpret the Nigeria application at the stated observational and modeling scope, including zero inflation, dependence and uncertainty. Do not infer causal effects from a regression fit or theoretical correctness from copied coefficients. Deliver the selected argument, exact source/data/environment identities, reproducible computations, a scientific discrepancy account with evidence and unresolved gaps. Lean is not required. No cached fit output, operator failure analysis or evaluator-only value is supplied as an answer.
